build.name: rewrite
build.description: rewrite: CPU chrome, Servo and Wasm engines in sig's process, no IPC

definition.description: rewrite: CPU chrome, Servo and Wasm engines in sig's process, no IPC

build.config:
# sig's configuration for benchmark runs of the rewrite, in the format of decision 28
# (version 1: bindings in [keys], not the baseline's [ui.keys]). The same keys do the same
# things as in baseline.config.toml, because the interaction scripts press them. bench/measure
# replaces "{workloads}" with the absolute path of bench/workloads.
version = 1

[keys]
"ctrl-l" = "location.focus"
"ctrl-tab" = "tab.next"
"ctrl-q" = "browser.quit"
"ctrl-t" = "tab.new"
"ctrl-w" = "tab.close"
"ctrl-o" = "page.open {workloads}/article.html"

home.description: Chrome only: sig's home page, no engine. Types into the URL bar.

article.description: Static Servo page: a text-heavy article with four images. Scrolls down, then up.

long.description: Scrolling a long text page (80 sections, ~26 000 words) with the mouse wheel.

css-animation.description: Servo: endless CSS transform, opacity, color and width animations. Pointer moves in the active window.

canvas.description: Servo: a 2D canvas redrawn every animation frame (300 balls). Pointer moves in the active window.

webgl.description: Servo: a WebGL quad rotating in 3D, redrawn every animation frame. Pointer moves in the active window.

wasm-hello.description: Wasm guest hello-sighurt: a static screen of canvas drawing and a text field, redrawn by on_frame at 60 Hz (the old sig-wasm sends a draw list only when it changed). Pointer moves in the active window.

wasm-gradient.description: Wasm guest gradient-demo: a static grid of gradients drawn with the canvas API. Pointer moves in the active window.

wasm-raf.description: Wasm guest raf-demo: a ball animated with request_animation_frame (animation). Pointer moves in the active window.

wasm-timer.description: Wasm guest timer-demo: idle in the steady window; in the active window its four buttons are clicked, starting set_interval timers of 1 s, 0.5 s and 0.1 s and a 3 s set_timeout.

wasm-busy.description: Plan §26's hostile Wasm workload: a guest (workloads/generate.py) that spends about 36M of its 50M fuel on every frame and draws one unchanging rectangle. Chrome input in the active window: a new tab and closing it again, twice a second.

many-tabs.description: Eight tabs of the article, one visible: what hidden tabs cost. Switches tab once a second in the active window.

tab-churn.description: Lifecycle: the article, then ten cycles of opening a new tab, loading the article in it and closing it (one every 2 s); measured again 3 s after the last close.

resize-storm.description: The article while the output changes size and scale four times a second (plan §25 resize storm); restored and measured 3 s later.

wasm-flood.description: Plan §26's output limits: a guest (workloads/generate.py) that draws 250 000 moving rectangles and writes 200 console lines on every frame, more than the rewrite's Wasm engine keeps. Chrome input in the active window: a new tab and closing it again, twice a second.

wasm-workers.description: Plan §26's worker fairness: a guest (workloads/generate.py) animating a square while four background workers each burn about 42M fuel per message, with eight messages queued each, so four threads stay busy. Chrome input in the active window: a new tab and closing it again, twice a second.
